text: People get better on the job. Most AI agents don't.
say: People get better on the job. Most A I agents don't.

text: That's the idea behind continual learning: keep learning from new experience, without forgetting what you already know.
say: That's the idea behind continual learning, keep learning from new experience, without forgetting what you already know.

text: The hard part is forgetting. You fix one failure, and something that used to work quietly breaks.
say: The hard part is forgetting. You fix one failure, and something that used to work quietly breaks.

text: Why? Your tasks share one prompt and one set of tools, so a fix for one task changes all of them.
say: Why? Your tasks share one prompt and one set of tools, so a fix for one task changes all of them.

text: So save each failure as a replayable eval, a test you can run again. Then improve the prompts, tools or memory.

text: Check every new fix against all your past evals. If they all pass, ship it. If one fails, back to the drawing board.

text: Continual learning in three rules. Agents don't learn on the job by default. A fix can quietly break an old skill. So save every failure as a test, and rerun them all before shipping.
